assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 100% increase from the same period last year, driven by a recent loss of U.S. measles elimination status.
Polio cases are peaking in Syria with circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 1 reported in Deir Ez Zor Governorate, while Wikipedia readership is rising.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with an 853% increase from the same period last year, though Wikipedia readership remains moderate.
Influenza activity is peaking globally with a 22% increase in flu test positivity and rising hospitalizations in the US, including a confirmed case of H5N1 in Washington State.
Mpox cases in the US are peaking with an 87% increase from the same period last year, though the number of cases has decreased compared to the previous year.
Whooping cough cases in the US are rising with a 55% increase from the same period last year, and news coverage has increased significantly.
West Nile virus cases in the US are rising with a 1388% increase from the same period last year, though the number of cases has decreased compared to the previous year.
Respiratory syncytial virus cases in the US are rising with a 57% increase in hospitalizations from the previous month.
US hospital admissions for COVID-19 are at baseline with a score of 60/100, showing a 13% monthly increase in admissions but higher news coverage and Wikipedia readership.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising with a 45% increase over 8 months, totaling 8,069 cases this year compared to 8,737 last year.
Chikungunya cases in the US are at baseline with a slight increase, but Switzerland reported its first locally acquired cases in October 2026.
Malaria cases in the US are at baseline with a 30% increase over 8 months, but the number of cases this year is lower than last year.
Cholera news coverage is rising with 1.6x the previous 4 weeks' coverage, but US cases remain at baseline.
Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) Wikipedia readership is at the 37th percentile of the past year, indicating rising interest.
Hepatitis A cases in the US are at baseline with a 10% increase over 8 months, but the number of cases this year is lower than last year.
